Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Time of day: cool white overhead light, flat and bright; flat white light with crisp edges, no warm glow.
Hair: her hair in a single loose braid over one shoulder — same colour and length as the attached image.

COMPOSITION: a close-up of her face and hair; body in side profile, her face in profile too, not turned toward the camera, facing the right of the frame, so her own right side is toward the camera; camera slightly above, looking down at her.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.

LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame — her far arm, on the side away from the camera.

EXPRESSION: one mouth corner lifted higher than the other, lips closed.

Framing: a close-up — her face and hair fill most of the frame and the bottom edge crosses at her collarbones; nothing below the shoulders shows, and her hands and anything she holds stay below the frame unless raised to her face.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — bohrium: a heavy synthetic metal below manganese, technetium and rhenium, first made in 1981 in a research city by striking bismuth with chromium ions, and named for the physicist of a harbour city who in 1913 pictured the atom as nested orbits stacked at fixed levels, where an electron may stand only on certain rings and gives off one exact colour of light whenever it leaps from one level down to another, explaining the red, cyan and violet lines of glowing hydrogen; first proposed under his full name, then shortened, though it sounds like boron; its longest-lived forms last only seconds to minutes — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.
